summary: Verified Pari's TTS voice feature end-to-end. Backend: 5/5 pytest tests pass for POST /api/interview-sim/tts (unauth, missing text, first-call, repeat-call cached=true, invalid-voice fallback). Audio is valid mp3 (ID3/0xFF frame sync, >1KB). Frontend: logged in as mocktest@valuevade.test, pushed attempt through application -> aptitude via API (frontend-driven flow validated separately for Apply-now navigation), then landed on HR (behavioural) round and verified: (a) interview-voice-toggle badge visible + defaults ON, (b) POST /api/interview-sim/tts fires automatically when the first interviewer question renders (200 OK), (c) interview-replay-* button visible ONLY on the latest interviewer turn, (d) amber 'Browser blocked auto-play — hit Replay to hear the question' warning renders because Playwright Chromium blocks autoplay (graceful fallback works), (e) clicking Replay fires another POST /api/interview-sim/tts (cached response, instant), (f) toggling voice OFF hides the Replay button, toggling ON brings it back without auto-replay (expected behaviour), (g) typing an answer + submitting still works and the next interviewer question fires 2 new TTS calls (req+resp) automatically. NO console errors during voice playback. TTS endpoint was NOT called during the aptitude phase (verified — 0 tts calls before HR stage).
critical_code_review_comments: interview_sim_endpoints.py:1203 — _TTS_CACHE is an in-process dict scoped to the closure of register_interview_sim_endpoints. Cache is not shared across worker processes (uvicorn --workers >1) but is fine for the current single-worker setup. Consider Redis-backed cache if scaled out.

interview_sim_endpoints.py:1206 — TTS endpoint has no per-user rate limit. A malicious client could burn Emergent-LLM-key credits by sending many distinct texts. Consider a simple per-user rate limit (e.g., 30 unique-text calls per minute).

useInterviewerVoice.js:87-97 — auto-play effect uses spokenIndexRef to avoid re-narrating; but if the last interviewer turn's index equals a previously-narrated one (e.g., after replacing the array with an equal-length one from server begin resume), the guard could over-suppress. Current UX is fine because turns only grow, but noting for future refactors.
InterviewStage.jsx:120-125 — lastInterviewerIdx recomputed inside .map for each turn (O(n^2)). For a 4-8 turn round this is negligible; keeping the note for larger transcripts.
Overall: implementation is clean, well-scoped, and the graceful-degradation path (autoplay-blocked -> Replay) is well-executed.
